about: What real machines, and the people using them, showed must change in Windstorm Mirror for GitHub, and the version each change is due in. A lesson here is a gate, not a note: tests/test_mirror.py (class Promises) refuses a version while a row due in it is not built, and refuses the version after it until the row says where it was proven on a real machine.
how_to_use: A new lesson gets a row the day it is learned: what was seen, the promise, a codon in DNA-STRAND-MASTER-PLAN.md, the version it is due in, and a tracking issue.
When it is built: put the name of its test in 'test'. The test must exist and be named in the plan next to the codon.

When it has been seen to work on a real machine: say which kind of machine, which version and when in 'proven'. A row whose test leans on a stand-in for GitHub, git, Gitea or Claude Code is seen for real before the tag of its version, not after.

'ship_in' moves only with a reason in 'moved_why'. A row whose owner is 'person' was seen by the person the skill is for, on their own machine: its date moves only by their word, restated in 'moved_by_person'.
A row is never deleted. A promise that turns out wrong is closed by a row that says why.
A lesson that was heard and not taken goes under 'declined' with the reason, so that nothing is dropped without a word.

rows.seen: 2026-10-23, a Git mirror of about 140 repositories that an AI agent ran every day from August to November 2026 on a shared Linux workstation, on stock Gitea beside GitHub: Gitea's own pull mirror had written the GitHub key into about 125 repositories' git config, readable by every account on the machine; it happened twice more after the clean-up, one exposure lasting about a day. 2026-11-22, our lab: stock Gitea 28.4.0 from the official binary in a Linux test account: the newest Gitea still did it (mode 664).
rows.promise: The GitHub key is never given to Gitea and never written into any git config: the skill fetches with the key in that one process's environment, and status scans every repository config for key shapes.
rows.proven: 2026-11-22, a Linux test account with no administrator rights, against the real GitHub on a private proof repository holding made-up data, with a broad GitHub login standing in for the read-only key the skill asks for: after four syncs, the key was found in none of the 4,201 files the account held (the forge's data, every repository config, the logs included).

rows.seen: a Git mirror of about 140 repositories that an AI agent ran every day from August to November 2026 on a shared Linux workstation, on stock Gitea beside GitHub: removing those keys froze more than a hundred private mirrors and nothing said so; Gitea raised no alarm when a mirror stopped refreshing, and mirrors marked 'known stale' sat frozen for weeks.
rows.promise: A copy that cannot refresh is never shown as current, for any reason; there is no 'known stale' pardon.

rows.seen: 2026-08-13, a Git mirror of about 140 repositories that an AI agent ran every day from August to November 2026 on a shared Linux workstation, on stock Gitea beside GitHub: mirrors pointed from the copy to GitHub would have force-written a stale copy over live work on their timer; removed before they fired.
rows.promise: Nothing is ever written to GitHub: no push, no push mirror, no API call that changes anything there.

rows.seen: 2026-11-22, our lab: stock Gitea 28.4.0 from the official binary in a Linux test account: a force-push or branch deletion on the source was erased from the copy at the next sync. a Git mirror of about 140 repositories that an AI agent ran every day from August to November 2026 on a shared Linux workstation, on stock Gitea beside GitHub: deleting branches the source had dropped found 2,053 such branches, 22 of which had to be kept because the copy might hold the last copy of their commits.
rows.promise: Before a branch or tag in the copy is moved backwards, rewritten or deleted, its old commit is kept under kept/<date>/<name>.
rows.proven: 2026-11-22, a Linux test account with no administrator rights, against the real GitHub on a private proof repository holding made-up data, with a broad GitHub login standing in for the read-only key the skill asks for: a branch forced back on GitHub was followed by the copy at the next sync, 8 s later, and its old commit was kept in the copy as kept/2026-11-22/lab8.

rows.seen: a Git mirror of about 140 repositories that an AI agent ran every day from August to November 2026 on a shared Linux workstation, on stock Gitea beside GitHub: a hand-kept list of repositories missed 130 active ones; a listing capped at 300 would have silently cut a larger account short.
rows.promise: Every repository is found by asking GitHub page by page to the last page; a failed page stops the listing rather than acting on half a list.

rows.seen: 2026-10-10 and 2026-10-21, a Git mirror of about 140 repositories that an AI agent ran every day from August to November 2026 on a shared Linux workstation, on stock Gitea beside GitHub: one hung fetch held every repository behind it for 5 to 10 minutes.
rows.promise: Every fetch and push has a time limit and one retry; one slow repository is named and never holds up the rest.

rows.seen: 2026-11-06, a Git mirror of about 140 repositories that an AI agent ran every day from August to November 2026 on a shared Linux workstation, on stock Gitea beside GitHub: a repository renamed on GitHub, and an old repository whose name was reused, nearly sent one project's history onto another; Gitea answered an old name with a redirect.
rows.promise: A repository is known by GitHub's numeric id; a rename renames the copy, and a reused name moves the old copy aside, never over it.

rows.seen: a Git mirror of about 140 repositories that an AI agent ran every day from August to November 2026 on a shared Linux workstation, on stock Gitea beside GitHub: the lesson of its months of use: a key that can write leaves GitHub open to the copy's mistakes, and a key shared with other tools runs out of allowance and is changed for reasons that have nothing to do with the copy.
rows.promise: The skill asks for read-only keys of its own, one per owner, and names a key that can write for what it is.

rows.seen: a Git mirror of about 140 repositories that an AI agent ran every day from August to November 2026 on a shared Linux workstation, on stock Gitea beside GitHub: the hourly GitHub API allowance ran out (about 3,900 of 5,000 calls an hour used), and a partial answer was once read as complete.
rows.promise: A sync counts its API calls and stops listing, and says so, below a floor of GitHub's remaining allowance.

rows.seen: a Git mirror of about 140 repositories that an AI agent ran every day from August to November 2026 on a shared Linux workstation, on stock Gitea beside GitHub: a check for keys on disk reported '0 found' because it had searched nothing.
rows.promise: The key scan counts the files it read; a scan that read none is a failure, not a pass.

rows.seen: a Git mirror of about 140 repositories that an AI agent ran every day from August to November 2026 on a shared Linux workstation, on stock Gitea beside GitHub: printing a Gitea config file put a secret into a log.
rows.promise: No key, password or whole config file is ever printed or logged; settings are read by name.

rows.seen: a Git mirror of about 140 repositories that an AI agent ran every day from August to November 2026 on a shared Linux workstation, on stock Gitea beside GitHub: after a reboot a timer showed 'active' with no next run for 3 hours.
rows.promise: After a reboot, status reads the timer's next run, not only whether it is switched on.

rows.seen: a Git mirror of about 140 repositories that an AI agent ran every day from August to November 2026 on a shared Linux workstation, on stock Gitea beside GitHub: the sync script was replaced by a deploy while it was running.
rows.promise: self-update replaces the skill's files whole, in one rename, and never while a sync runs.

rows.seen: a Git mirror of about 140 repositories that an AI agent ran every day from August to November 2026 on a shared Linux workstation, on stock Gitea beside GitHub: no one ever recovered a project from that mirror alone; its drill restored the forge's own database from a backup.
rows.promise: restore --check proves every copy from the forge alone, with no network beyond this computer: every branch and tag against the refs last seen on GitHub, and git fsck.

rows.seen: a Git mirror of about 140 repositories that an AI agent ran every day from August to November 2026 on a shared Linux workstation, on stock Gitea beside GitHub: the hourly GitHub API allowance ran out (about 3,900 of 5,000 calls an hour used), and a partial answer was once read as complete.
rows.promise: A sync fetches only the repositories whose pushed_at changed since their last good refresh; a daily full pass fetches all; a quiet sync costs one listing call per 100 repositories per owner.
rows.proven: 2026-11-22, a Linux test account with no administrator rights, against the real GitHub on a private proof repository holding made-up data, with a broad GitHub login standing in for the read-only key the skill asks for: a sync with nothing changed on GitHub spent 1 API call and fetched nothing; after a force-push, the next sync fetched that repository.

rows.seen: 2026-11-22, the first real setup of this skill, in a Linux test account with no administrator rights: Gitea's download site answered 403 Forbidden to Python's default User-Agent, so setup stopped before anything was installed (an AI agent running a long-lived mirror had seen the same kind of block on another site before).
rows.promise: The download names the skill in its User-Agent, and a refused download says what was refused and that nothing was run.
rows.proven: 2026-11-22, a Linux test account with no administrator rights: with the named User-Agent, setup downloaded Gitea 28.4.0 and its checksum matched the pin.

rows.seen: 2026-11-22, the first real setup of this skill, in a Linux test account with no administrator rights, stock Gitea 28.4.0: a repository created through the API with no 'private' field came out public, although the forge's setting DEFAULT_PRIVATE was 'private' (that setting only fills in the web form).
rows.promise: Every copy is created with private set to true, and the answer is checked: a copy that came out public is made private, or setup stops and says so.

rows.seen: 2026-11-22, a Mac on Intel (macOS 13), FileVault off, with the system logging its account in by itself: after a restart, two launch agents in that account came back with no one at the keyboard, the service-like one 45 s after the boot and the interval one on its interval. Until then the skill said, on every Mac, that the copy stands still until the person logs in.
rows.promise: On a Mac, the skill says the copy comes back by itself after a restart only when the system logs the person in by itself; otherwise it says the copy stands still until they log in.
